patch.summary: ClickUp migration guide: inventory → rehearse → freeze → validate integrations — grounded in researched limitations and catalogue peers.

blocks.body: Migrate to ClickUp by inventorying legacy project-management fields, mapping them to ClickUp objects, rehearsing a freeze window, and validating Slack, Google Workspace, Github before reopening writes.
bullets: Inventory → map → rehearse → cut over → reopen
Highest risk: Configuration sprawl without admin standards
Success signal: task boards works for the pilot cohort

blocks.heading: ClickUp migration cutover playbook
blocks.body: Migrations fail from optimistic timelines — not from missing motivation.

scenarios.title: Field inventory
scenarios.body: Export legacy fields that power task boards, timeline / Gantt, workload and resources and mark must-map vs archive.

scenarios.title: Rehearsal load
scenarios.body: Run a non-prod load into ClickUp; measure match rates before the freeze.

scenarios.title: Production freeze
scenarios.body: Freeze legacy writes; cut over; validate Slack; then reopen.

steps.label: Migrate when Teams consolidating tasks+docs+dashboards outweigh migration cost
Delay if this limitation hits cutover: Configuration sprawl without admin standards
If ClickUp mapping is poor, compare destination fit with Asana before moving data twice

items.title: No freeze window
items.body: Dual-writing without a freeze creates irrevocable duplicates.

items.title: Integrations last
items.body: Wire Slack in rehearsal — not on Monday morning after cutover.

items.title: Data risk 2
items.body: AI Brain packaging can add cost beyond Unlimited floors

items.title: Data risk 3
items.body: Steeper onboarding than Asana for non-technical teams

checklist.label: Complete field inventory for task boards
Mitigate: Configuration sprawl without admin standards

notes: Migration: cutover risks, data mapping, checklist.
